title: Production run watch (hourly)
description:
Purpose: hourly read-only watch of production for failures and missing outputs, filing one deduped issue per job and symptom.
Trigger: weekdays hourly on cron `25 * * * 1-5` (Europe/Rome) and every 2h at `:25` on weekends on cron `25 */2 * * 0,6` (UTC); each tick covers the last 2h.
Inputs: GitHub Actions on `develop` and `main` (digithings-ai/digithings); Cloudflare Workers (digithings-cron clocks, digiquant-runner house run, digithings-digichat, dashboard-api, other prod Workers); the published outputs; the `digithings-operating-rules` "Run watch" section.
Do:
1. GitHub Actions: `gh run list -b develop -L 50 --json databaseId,name,conclusion,createdAt` and the same for `main`. Flag any `failure`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure`, and read `gh run view <id> --log-failed`.
2. Cloudflare Workers: use the Cloudflare observability tools, or `wrangler tail` / observability queries read-only, for errors and exceptions.
3. Check outputs, not just exit codes: the house run (Mon-Fri) has a committed book (core positions dated today) and a `success.json` in the archive; DataTap answer-integrity hourly green; provider review green; twelve-x feed published. On Mondays also confirm the house run before 13:30 UTC.
4. Ignore the known noise: the weekly continuous-improvement digest (standing note) and main's gitleaks red on the 2 known leaks.
5. Per failure, build the dedupe key `run-watch:<job>:<symptom>` and search open issues for `[run-watch] <job>`. If one exists, COMMENT the new occurrence (run id, time, log excerpt) there. Otherwise open ONE issue.
Output: one issue `[run-watch] <job>: <symptom>` in project digithings with evidence (run id, log lines), root cause, proposed fix and the dedupe key — plus a comment on this run issue naming what was filed and where. Assign the owning seat: digiquant/house run → Quant; Workers/cron/edge → Backend Engineer, Reliability or Edge & Domains Engineer; CI/workflows → Repo, CI & Release Engineer; DataTap → FDE DataTap. The assignee opens a fix PR into `develop` and owns it until merged.
Silent if: nothing failed and every output above is verified with only the two known-noise items present — no issue, no comment; close this run issue with the one line "all green" and no other tickets.
Owner / Consumer: Owner Backend 2 (`d82a8a95-a998-4ab7-b62e-87ee06533312`); consumer the owning seat assigned per filed issue, which owns the fix PR until merged.
Never: re-run, re-kick, redeploy or roll back anything in production without Chris.
COST RULE: never curl `digithings.ai/api/health`, `/embed` or `/api/chat`, or `graph.`/`key.`/`search.digithings.ai`, to check liveness — these wake paid containers. Check those Workers only through Cloudflare observability and `wrangler containers list`. `digithings-cron` and `dashboard-api` `/healthz` are fine.

title: twelve-x: confirm daily that the research feed published what it should have
description:
Purpose: confirm daily the twelve-x research feed published one fx_daily_digest row per trading date.
Trigger: cron 0 9 * * *.
Inputs: /Users/chrisstefan/Code/twelve-x at origin/develop, .env/.venv, scripts/confirm_feed_published.py.
Do: run verbatim, byte-for-byte; never fetch, retype, paraphrase. Only REF= parameterised (REF=develop). Do not retype, reorder, simplify or hand-edit dates:
REPO=/Users/chrisstefan/Code/twelve-x
REF=develop
SCRIPT=scripts/confirm_feed_published.py
ENVFILE="$REPO/.env"
test -f "$ENVFILE" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (no $ENVFILE)"; exit 2; }
test -x "$REPO/.venv/bin/python" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (no .venv in $REPO)"; exit 2; }
cd "$REPO" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2"; exit 2; }
git fetch --quiet origin "$REF" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (fetch)"; exit 2; }
RUNNER=$(mktemp -t confirm_feed_published)
git show "origin/${REF}:${SCRIPT}" > "$RUNNER" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (${SCRIPT} not on origin/${REF})"; rm -f "$RUNNER"; exit 2; }
SINCE=$(date -u -v-2d +%Y-%m-%d)
UNTIL=$(date -u -v-1d +%Y-%m-%d)
set -a; . "$ENVFILE"; set +a
.venv/bin/python "$RUNNER" --since "$SINCE" --until "$UNTIL"
code=$?
rm -f "$RUNNER"
echo "confirm-feed: exit $code"
exit $code
Verdict: 0 = window covered, no gaps, no escalation. 1 = ONE child of DIG-216 per gap finding, assigned FDE twelve-x, naming the missing trading date and what you checked; broken run = DIG-693's - do not close. 2 = could not run - report why; an unrun check is not a passed check; never print/paste the Supabase service key.

Honesty: expected dates 0 (every Monday pass - [today-2, today-1] covers Sat/Sun only) = vacuous, confirmed nothing; never report the feed healthy. A vacuous pass is not evidence.
Scope: one fx_daily_digest row per trading date, three sessions collapsed (London publishing while Asia and New York did not still counts as published). Does not check content correctness; no session attribution (pass --runs); no FX session calendar (without --calendar a holiday reads as a gap).
Silent if: exit 0 with expected dates > 0 - nothing filed, nothing escalated.
Owner / Consumer: FDE twelve-x runs it; DIG-1073, DIG-693 owners and the client-commitment record read it. Continue until BOTH: DIG-693 landed AND the check wired to page a human on its own (the merge alone is not a stand-down).

description:

2. Start from the real count: `gh issue list --repo digithings-ai/twelve-x --label daily-run-failure --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,body,createdAt`. 4. A `daily-run-failure` title does not name its region: read the body's `- Workflow:` line and the run URL before grouping.
5. Per open occurrence, in order: attribute it (run URL, failing job, one-line root cause); if a tracked issue already carries that cause, comment `Duplicate of DIG-nnn - <one-line cause>. Closed by the DIG-228 daily sweep.`, close it, then comment the same line on the tracking issue; if it shares a signature with an occurrence opened in the last 24h, keep the earliest open as the occurrence of record and close the later ones against it with the same comment format (pre-window, hand-filed and non-WINDOW_MS filings, since DIG-286 folds them into `Another occurrence within the 24h window.`); if you cannot attribute it, do not close it - escalate.

Escalation: at most one Paperclip issue per day, high, assigned to yourself, only for a signature no tracked issue covers, one appearing >3 times in 24h, or an occurrence resembling a client-visible data gap - read the window comments before deciding none fired; name the decision and the evidence, never one per occurrence. title: twelve-x: run the develop merge queue on a cadence
description:
You are the merge-queue driver for `digithings-ai/twelve-x` `develop`. This routine exists because [DIG-506](/DIG/issues/DIG-506) built the runner (`scripts/merge_queue.py`, commit `e616ee4a4`) and nothing ran it. The queue grew from 11 to 14 eligible PRs while it sat idle.

**No decision card is required to merge a green leaf PR.** That is the whole point. If you find yourself thinking one is needed, you have misread the gate list below. Do not route it to Chris. Do not ask the CTO for per-merge approval.

## What you run

Copy this block **verbatim**.

> 2026-10-17 (Chris): the `--attest-review qa` flag was removed from this block. Do not add it back; QA posts its own `qa/gate` commit status. Do not retype it, do not reorder it, do not raise `--max-merges`, and do not add `--admin`.

The block fetches THREE runner files and passes `--limit 40`: without `check_review_coverage.py` the run dies with `ModuleNotFoundError`, and at the default `--limit 50` the single `gh pr list` requests ~525,100 nodes and GitHub refuses it (`exceeds the maximum limit of 500,000`). See DIG-3240.

```bash
REPO=digithings-ai/twelve-x
ROLE=em
GIT_DIR=/Users/chrisstefan/code/digithings
WORK="$PAPERCLIP_RUN_SCRATCH_DIR/merge-queue"

mkdir -p "$WORK"
git -C "$GIT_DIR" fetch github develop --quiet
git -C "$GIT_DIR" show github/develop:scripts/merge_queue.py       > "$WORK/merge_queue.py"
git -C "$GIT_DIR" show github/develop:scripts/merge_queue_policy.json > "$WORK/merge_queue_policy.json"
git -C "$GIT_DIR" show github/develop:scripts/check_review_coverage.py   > "$WORK/check_review_coverage.py"

# One merge per invocation, so the base moves only once between merges.
python3 "$WORK/merge_queue.py" run \
  --repo "$REPO" --acting-role "$ROLE" --max-merges 1 --limit 40
```

Report the output verbatim in a comment on the run issue, then close the run issue.

## Reading the outcome

| Exit | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| 0, printed `merged #N` | A merge landed | Comment the output, close the run issue. |
| 0, printed `nothing merged` | Nothing was eligible | Close the run issue. Not a failure. |
| 1 | `gh` could not read the queue | Comment it, leave the run issue open. |
| 2 | Role not on the roster | Comment it, close the run issue. A refusal, not a retry. |
| 3 | Base is `main`/`master`/`release/*` | Comment it, close the run issue. A refusal, not a retry. |

## Do not merge faster than CI

**One merge per run. That is the rate limit, and it is not conservative.**

`merge_queue.py` refuses a PR whose `mergeStateStatus` is `BEHIND`, because after a merge the next PR's green `test` is the run against the *previous* base. That gate is the whole reason this queue is safe. If a single run merged a batch, every PR after the first would be merged on stale evidence. `run` re-reads the queue after each merge so the queue stops and reports instead of sending a stale-base merge — that is correct behaviour, not a bug.

Observed on this repo: the `test` check takes ~60s, and a PR becomes eligible again roughly 90–120s after the base moves. So one PR per run, and the run cadence sets the merge rate.

## What you do not do

- **No workflow files, settings, rulesets, secrets or branch protection in `twelve-x`.** It is a client repo. The runner acts through the GitHub API from our own checkout and needs nothing in the client repo.
- **Never `--admin`.** The runner already refuses to pass it. If a PR only merges with admin, that is a blocker to report, not a step to take.
- **Never edit `scripts/merge_queue_policy.json`.** Adding a role is a policy change for the CTO. Editing the file at all is out of scope.
- Never push to `develop` directly. The queue governs the merge path; a direct push bypasses every gate.

## When something is blocked

`run` prints the blocked list with a reason per PR. For a PR that has been blocked for more than two consecutive runs, post the handback on the PR itself naming the specific gate — `CONFLICTING`, `BEHIND`/stale `test`, a failing check, or missing review — and open an issue for the owning agent. A blocked PR gets handed back with a reason, not left sitting silently.

`docs/MERGE_QUEUE.md` and `scripts/merge_queue_policy.json` on `develop` are the gate definition and the roster.

title: twelve-x: confirm daily that the research feed published what it should have
description:
You own the daily confirmation of what the twelve-x research feed actually published. This is the holder for a commitment the client has been given in writing: until the loud-failure check lands, we go and confirm for them that "the feed looks fine".

This exists because of [DIG-700](/DIG/issues/DIG-700). Counsel refused to clear the SEV2 note while it carried an unowned promise of ongoing manual service. Owning it means this routine, on a clock, with your name on it.

DIG-700 is closed — its question was answered, not its work finished. **Report findings here, not there.** This routine is homed under [DIG-216](/DIG/issues/DIG-216), because it is the manual stand-in for exactly the measurement DIG-216 owes: what the Hub can actually serve, rather than what our internal records received. When DIG-216 lands and is wired to a human, this routine stands down.

### What you run

Copy this block **verbatim**. Do not retype it, do not reorder it, do not "simplify" it, do not substitute `make`, and do not hand-edit the dates.

```bash
REPO=/Users/chrisstefan/Code/twelve-x
REF=develop
SCRIPT=scripts/confirm_feed_published.py
ENVFILE="$REPO/.env"

test -f "$ENVFILE" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (no $ENVFILE)"; exit 2; }
test -x "$REPO/.venv/bin/python" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (no .venv in $REPO)"; exit 2; }

cd "$REPO" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2"; exit 2; }
git fetch --quiet origin "$REF" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (fetch)"; exit 2; }

RUNNER=$(mktemp -t confirm_feed_published)
git show "origin/${REF}:${SCRIPT}" > "$RUNNER" || { echo "confirm-feed: exit 2 (${SCRIPT} not on origin/${REF})"; rm -f "$RUNNER"; exit 2; }

# Confirm the previous two days: today and yesterday by UTC, so a digest that lands
# after the run clock is still caught by tomorrow's pass.
SINCE=$(date -u -v-2d +%Y-%m-%d)
UNTIL=$(date -u -v-1d +%Y-%m-%d)

set -a; . "$ENVFILE"; set +a
.venv/bin/python "$RUNNER" --since "$SINCE" --until "$UNTIL"
code=$?
rm -f "$RUNNER"
echo "confirm-feed: exit $code"
exit $code
```

The block ends in `exit $code`, so it is usable as-is in any runner that reads an exit status. The echo line is for the human reading the issue.

### The ref, and why it is now `develop`

`REF=develop`. The single-line migration is **done** (FDE twelve-x, 2026-10-07).

The block was authored on the branch `DIG-594-counsel-the-post-incident-note-can-no-longer-be-standalone-it-must-deal-with-line-09-and-counsel-has-to-see-the-`. PR digithings-ai/twelve-x#264 merged that branch into `develop` at 2026-10-05T15:35:01Z and the branch was then deleted on the remote, so the old value stopped resolving. With `REF` still on the branch, every pass died at `git fetch` with `confirm-feed: exit 2 (fetch)` — before reading the table, so it measured nothing at all. Verified on 2026-10-07 before changing anything: `fatal: couldn't find remote ref DIG-594-...`, exit 2.

After the change the block was run once by hand, as required: `exit 0`, window `2026-10-05 .. 2026-10-06`, `expected dates: 2`, `published digests: 2`. `scripts/confirm_feed_published.py` is present on `origin/develop`.

**Do not change `REF` back or on to anything else, and do not add a fallback that tries one ref then another.** A check that silently changes what it is checking is the thing this routine exists to stop. `main` is the release branch and lags `develop`; do not point at it.

The last line is the verdict. Exit 0 clean, exit 1 gaps, exit 2 the check could not run.

**Why the env file is sourced rather than loaded.** `.env` is gitignored and lives only in the main checkout. `config.py` wants `TWELVEX_SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`. Do not echo it, do not print it, do not paste it anywhere. If it is missing, exit 2 and say so on the issue; do not proceed with a partial check.

The script asks one question per trading date: does `fx_daily_digest` hold a row for that `run_date`. That is deliberately a different measurement from [DIG-216](/DIG/issues/DIG-216), which asks whether internal records received new entries and cannot see a run that selected 42 files, kept 4 of which none was research, wrote no digest, and reported success, and was never retried.

### When it finds a gap

1. Open a **new** issue as a child of [DIG-216](/DIG/issues/DIG-216) with the date, the finding kind, and what you already checked. Say plainly whether anything was published for that date. One issue per finding, so each date stands on its own.
2. Do not close it yourself if the cause is a broken run. That is [DIG-693](/DIG/issues/DIG-693)'s work and its owner's.
3. If the date is a market holiday, the finding is the calendar's fault, not the feed's. Record it and open the calendar ticket.
4. If the script itself exits 2, that is a finding too. A check that cannot run is not a check that passed.

### What this confirmation covers, and what it does not

Read this before you report anything to a human. It is the difference between an owned commitment and a wider one nobody agreed to.

**It covers: did a date the client was owed actually reach them.** One digest row per trading date, all three sessions collapsed. If London published and Asia and New York did not, the client still got that date's feed and there is no client-visible gap. Do not go looking for per-session failures and report them as breaches of this routine. The session field on a finding is there to help diagnosis, not to widen the claim.

Counsel asked which sessions this watches, and the honest answer is: **all three, jointly, measured on the one surface the client reads.** A check that demanded all three sessions independently would be measuring our pipeline, which is [DIG-693](/DIG/issues/DIG-693)'s job, not this routine's.

**It does not cover content that published under the wrong date.** Six of the twelve stale days were recovered under a later date: the documents arrived, the digest existed, and it was labelled wrong. A presence check cannot see that, because the digest row is there. This is a real blind spot and the note tells the client about those days.

Nobody can close that blind spot by reading harder. The pipeline logged each file's id and never its publication date, so per-document attribution for those days is unrecoverable from the records we kept. Catching mis-dating from now on needs the pipeline to record what it published and when, which is the [DIG-216](/DIG/issues/DIG-216) change the note already promises. Until that lands, do not claim this routine confirms the right content landed on the right day. It confirms the client was not left with a hole.

If someone asks you to confirm content correctness, the answer is that this routine does not do it and why.

### Two limits you must not paper over

- **No session attribution on the Hub surface.** No table in this project carries a session column and `fx_daily_digest` is one row per `run_date`. If you need to name the session behind a gap, export the workflow runs and pass `--runs`. The client was told about London, New York and Asia days, so a gap you cannot attribute is a gap you must still report.
- **No FX session calendar in this repository.** Without `--calendar`, expected dates are weekdays, so a holiday reads as a gap. The script prints which basis it used. Do not quietly present a weekday-rule run as calendar-accurate.

### How long this runs

Until [DIG-693](/DIG/issues/DIG-693) lands **and** this check is wired to something that pages a human on its own. Landing the loud-failure check ends the reason for manual confirmation. It does not end this routine on its own. Do not stand this down because the fix merged; stand it down when a real replacement is reading the signal.

Our own evidence for why: the PrimeMarket detector ran 29 consecutive failing times over 14 days and alerted nobody ([DIG-526](/DIG/issues/DIG-526)), and the answer-integrity detector filed a repo issue nobody read for 16 days. A red run is not a page. You are the page.

The second promise in the note, the credential rule, is not yours. It is [DIG-377](/DIG/issues/DIG-377), held by IT support.

title: Monthly secret ageing by hand (DIG-477 option D)
description:
Age every GitHub Actions secret name against the 90-day rotation window, by hand, on the Mac.

Paperclip DIG-477 option D (Chris, 2026-10-05) took the ageing half out of CI: the Actions secrets
endpoints need a token with the `repo` scope and a workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` never has one, so the
monthly CI run of the same script does the environment-gate drift half only, via `--gates-only`.
Rotation is a human decision from here. This routine is that decision's owner and cadence.

Do these steps in this order:

1. Check out the digithings repo on the Mac and `make secrets-staleness`, which runs
   `scripts/secret_staleness_check.py --open-issue`. Use a shell whose `gh auth` already carries
   `repo` and `admin:org`. If the token lacks a scope, the run says which level was unavailable.
   Say so in the comment rather than reporting the unreadable level as empty.
2. Read the report. It lists every repo, org and `cron`-environment secret name with its
   last-written date. It reads no secret value; GitHub does not return values on that endpoint.
   Never print a value.
3. Update `docs/ops/SECRETS_INVENTORY.md` with the current count and the current list of overdue
   names, replacing the previous month's numbers. Open a PR for it. A month where nothing crossed
   the window is a recorded zero, not a missing entry.
4. Comment on the issue with: the count of listed names, the count past the window, the oldest
   names with their ages, and whether the PR for the inventory update opened.
5. If any name is more than 180 days old, open an issue for Chris naming the secret name only,
   and say plainly what is lost if it stays: `token-canary.yml` probes only `DIGITHINGS_PROJECT_TOKEN`
   and `GH_DISPATCH_TOKEN` daily, so the other overdue names have no automated liveness check.

Not to do:

- Do not add, move or delete any secret value. Only Chris can, and #248 handles that.
- Do not touch `production`.
- Do not automate this from CI. Do not add a permission to `secret-staleness-check.yml`; there is
  no value of `permissions:` that can read secrets.
- Do not name the Keymaster weekly key report as a source for this. That report is built from
  Bitwarden and never reads the GitHub Actions secrets API. A claim to the contrary was propagated
  into five files and had to be retracted in PR #5078.

If a step fails, open an issue for the CTO with the exact error text in it.

title: Monthly rate-versus-billed review
description:
# Monthly rate-versus-billed review

**Owner**: FP&A Analyst (`1fb2f1ea-00aa-415d-9c05-c07c04949c68`). **Cadence**: monthly, first working day after month end, Europe/Rome. **Built from**: DIG-1746 (CFO).

## What this is for
Every month, check the rate actually realised on the work we billed, against the rate the market would bear for that same scope. Output is advice to Chris. Never an automatic price change.

The business does **not** bill by the hour. See "Denominator rule" below — do not invent an hourly rate.

## Step 0 — decide the period (do this first)
1. Period just closed = the calendar month that ended most recently.
2. Billing period = `standing.md` line 18: ongoing work is billed **every two months**, itemised on what was delivered. So the run reviews the **billing period that the closed month falls in**, not the calendar month.
3. **Never-reviewed wins over recent.** Take the most recent billing period that has a **live** ledger row (status `paid` or `draft` — not `void`) **and has not yet been reviewed**. A period already reviewed is skipped, so nothing is double counted. But a billing period that carries a live row and was never reviewed must be picked up even if it is not the newest one — that is how a price decision that sat unshipped gets reviewed instead of being skipped forever.
4. Read `clients/pipeline.csv` for the billing window. If the ledger has no live row for any unreviewed billing period, say so and stop — that is a valid result, and it means "no realised rate to measure this month".
5. **Only a live row is measurable.** Void rows and superseded drafts are not figures. Never compute a rate from a void row, even when it is the most recent row for that client.

## Step 1 — compute the realised rate
Read both, every time:
- `dt-books status`
- `~/digithings-books/ledger/invoices.csv`

### Denominator rule
The books hold **no delivered hours**. There is no timesheet anywhere in `~/digithings-books`. They hold **itemised scope value in USD**. So the denominator is **delivered scope**. Never state or estimate an hourly rate — there is no basis for one.

Two computable metrics:
- **Recovery rate** = billed total ÷ scope subtotal. `80%` means a 20% discount was given. This is the realised rate.
- **Effective USD per billed line** = billed total ÷ number of billed lines. Use it only as a trend line across months, never as a rate for a quote.

Report recovery rate **per client** and **overall**. Client key only — the client is `twelve-x` or `DataTap`, never a legal entity name, never a person's name.

If a row in the ledger has a total but no subtotal (INV-2026-001 is like this), the scope basis is unknown. Report the total, mark recovery rate `UNKNOWN`, and move on. Do not estimate the missing subtotal.

## Step 2 — ask for the market band (ONE request, not a standing desk)
Open an issue to the **PM** (`e3051fec-c562-47eb-9f84-c43323b3c494`) asking for the current market band, and let the PM task its researcher.

Send the **PM**, not the Market Analyst, because Market Analyst is moving under PM on DIG-1704. This survives the reorg. If the PM is unavailable, the run waits; do not fall back to routing around the PM.

Give **scope, never the client name**. A request that reads:

> Market band for: building a modular agentic-AI platform — agent orchestration/runtime, CI and release engineering, documentation, and ongoing maintenance, sold as a fixed scope with itemised line values in USD. Bought by a small engineering team. Answer with a recommended discount band off the scope subtotal and your source.

That is the whole ask. No client name, no invoice number, no totals, no ledger path. If the answer needs client detail to be useful, it is the wrong question — the band is a property of the scope.

## Step 3 — write the comparison
Use this exact format. It is short. Keep it short.

```
## Rate vs billed — <billing period, e.g. Aug–Sep 2026>
Reviewed <date>. Source: `ledger/invoices.csv`, `dt-books status`.

**Market band (recommended discount)**: <low>–<high>% off scope subtotal — <PM>, <date>. Confidence: <CONFIRMED|LIKELY|UNSURE|UNKNOWN>
**Realised rate (recovery rate)**: <client> <x.x>% · overall <y.y>%
**Scope subtotal / billed total**: USD <a> / USD <b>
**Gap**: realised <x.x>% vs band <low>–<high>% → <n.n pp> <inside|below|above> band
**Change since last month**: <what moved, or "no change">
**Recommendation**: <one line>
Confidence: <label>
```

Rules for the format:
- Percentages to one decimal. Every EUR/USD figure to two decimals.
- "Gap" is stated in **percentage points against the band**, and says plainly which side of the band we are on. If we are inside the band, say so in those words.
- "Change since last month" is mandatory even when the answer is "no change".
- On the **first run** there is no prior month. Write the line as `first review — no prior month to compare`, and add one sentence on how many times the billing period's price moved before this review settled. That count is the finding, and it is computed from the live row plus the void/superseded rows of the same billing period, counting distinct totals only. Never quote a superseded total as if it were real; naming it as "a superseded draft that was never issued" is correct and is the point.
- One confidence label at the end of the block, not one per line.

## Step 4 — card to Chris when the gap is material
Material = realised rate outside the band by **more than 5 percentage points**, or any month-on-month move in the realised rate of more than 5 points. Post it as an `ask_user_questions` card on the run's issue, `resolverPolicy: human_only`.

A good card carries: the numbers, the recommended band, the gap, the one-line recommendation, and the confidence label. Card contents, in this order:
1. The question, in one sentence.
2. The numbers.
3. The recommendation.
4. Confidence label + source.

The card is **about the standing rate rule**, not about any single invoice. Chris has already decided the individual invoices; do not reopen a settled figure.

## Hard rules (these are not optional)
- **Price is never an auto-decision** — `~/paperclip-workspace/decisions/standing.md` line 17. Output is a card. Never write a rate into the ledger. Never edit `ledger/invoices.csv` to change a price.
- **Never draft or send anything to a client.** No quote, no covering email, no "here is your rate". `standing.md` line 20.
- **Never apply a rate, never file, never send, never pay.** Chris approves, sends, files and pays — line 5.
- **Before raising a card, check whether Chris already answered the same question on another card.** Line 26. The later clear answer wins. If he has answered, do not raise it again; record that he already answered and move on.
- **Never quote a dead figure.** Only figures traceable to a live ledger row or a live draft may appear. Numbers from voided invoices, superseded drafts, or struck line items are not real and must not appear.
- **Never tell anyone to find a human expert.** Line 6. Research the answer and label the confidence.
- **No bank, tax or ID numbers in any comment or card.** No IBAN, no VAT number, no fiscal code, no passport or ID numbers.
- **Tax is not this routine's job.** `dt-books status` is CONDITIONAL and its 15% line is arithmetic for visibility, not a computed liability. The forfettario availability question is open (adjudicated LIKELY, not CONFIRMED). If a rate discussion turns on tax, stop and ask Tax Specialist (`0be08f90-2593-48d5-bb18-98a441e19b8d`), carry its source and confidence label onto the card, and put **no sanction amount and no fine band** on it.
- **Client and finance data stays on zero-retention models only.** Line 4: free models are fine for finance and business work.
- **Never print, log or paste a secret.**

## Not to do
- Do not compute or quote an hourly rate. There are no hours in the books.
- Do not apply the recommended band to anything. Advise only.
- Do not treat a gap as material because it feels large — the test is 5 points.
- Do not open a per-client question to a client. This routine never talks to a client.
- Do not raise the forfettario question in a rate card.
- Do not re-raise a question Chris has already answered (`standing.md` line 26).

## Idempotency and the working-day rule
The trigger fires on days 1–3 of each month, Europe/Rome. **The first run of a calendar month is the review. Every later run in the same month exits immediately** with "period already reviewed on <date>" — that is the correct outcome, not a failure, and no card goes out.

**Working-day guard, applied before anything else.** The cadence is the *first working day* after month end, and the day-1–3 window sometimes opens on a weekend — 2026-11-01 is a Sunday. If the run's date in Europe/Rome is a **Saturday or Sunday**, or a public holiday, exit immediately with "not a working day — <date>" and let the next day inside the window carry the review. Do not mark the period reviewed, do not ask the PM for a band, do not raise a card. Working out the holiday calendar is not this run's job: a day that looks like a working day is treated as one, and the review is advisory and reversible.

## If a step fails
Open an issue for the **FP&A Analyst** with the exact error text and which step it died at. Do not guess past a missing number, and do not carry a half-computed recovery rate into a card.

## Sources
- `~/digithings-books/ledger/invoices.csv` — the only authority on what was billed.
- `~/digithings-books/clients/pipeline.csv` — billing window, client key.
- `dt-books status` — cash and tax context, every figure ESTIMATE ONLY.
- `~/paperclip-workspace/decisions/standing.md` — lines 5, 6, 17, 18, 20, 25 bind this routine.
- Market band comes from PM each run; it is never cached as a fact. Carry the answer's own date and confidence label into the comparison.
